questions.question:

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The laptop that I bought last week works __very good__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. **'****very well'.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in Part **(****very good****)** of the sentence.
 
• The structure of the given sentence is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence we have to **modify the verb 'works,'** and **an adverb modifies a verb.**
 
• Here** 'good' is not an adverb** but an adjective that can modify a noun.
 
• So we need to **replace 'good' with 'well' which is an adverb.**
 
• Therefore, the use of 'very good' in the sentence should be replaced with **'****very well****'** to make it grammatically correct.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Correct sentence:__ *The laptop that I bought last week works **__very well__.***

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

Don’t disturb me while I __talk__ to someone on the phone.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 2) i.e. '****am talking****'.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in Part **(****talk****)** of the sentence.
 
• The structure of the given sentence is incorrect.
 
• Here the given sentence is in **present tense** and **two actions are taking place** here **'****Don’t disturb me'** and** 'I am talking.'**
 
• In such cases **after 'while' we need to use the continuous form of the verb.**
 
• Therefore, we should remove** 'talk' (present form)** and use** 'am talking' (continuous form).**
 
• Therefore, the **use of '****talk****'**** **in the sentence **should be replaced with '**am talking**' **to make it grammatically correct**.**
 
• Therefore, the **correct answer is Option 2.**

 

**Correct sentence:**__ *Don’t disturb me while I __**am talking**__ to someone on the phone.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Reva is / one of Gita’s best friend / in the class.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 1) i.e. **‘****one of Gita’s best friend’.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in the part ‘one of Gita’s best friend’.
 
• According to the rules of subject-verb agreement, if **'each, every, one' is used after 'of,' then the 'noun and pronoun' followed by 'of' will be in the plural number.**
 
• **Example**:
 
 
• *​One of my friends works in the defence ministry.*
 
 
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we have to replace ‘one of Gita’s best friend’ with ‘one of Gita’s best friends’ to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct sentence:__ *Reva is **one of Gita’s best friends** in the class.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

I thanked my teacher for__ explaining me the lesson__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. **'****explaining the lesson to me'.**

 

***__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in Part **(****explaining me the lesson****)** of the sentence.
 
• The** structure** of the given sentence is incorrect.
 
• According to the rules of Prepositions, **after the verb 'explain'** we should **always use the preposition 'to' and the 'objective form of the subject.' **
 
• So we need to **remove 'me' after the verb 'explaining'** and **replace it with 'to me'.**
 
• Therefore, the use of **'****explaining me the lesson****'** in the sentence should be replaced with **'****explaining the lesson to me****'** to make it grammatically correct.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Correct sentence:__* I thanked my teacher for **__explaining the lesson to me.__***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• According to the rules of Prepositions, after the verbs 'explain, speak, reply, complain, talk, listen, write' we should always use the preposition 'to' and the 'objective form of the subject.' 
 
• **Example**:
 
 
• ​I am **grateful to** the judge for listening to me.*
